ideas.title: Sail it yourself, live: the 3D sail box rides with the cart
ideas.critique: This is the first time on the island that the player steers something whose force comes from a live 3D flow, and over-sheeting stalls because the flow stalls, not because a rule says so. After ten films of devices left alone, this is the strongest change of form on offer. The risk is that a 400k-cell box can't keep real time beside the frame, and a tabled fallback would bring it down to a 5-level rig.

ideas.title: Tack up the beach: the friends cross the deck at every turn
ideas.critique: Having the crew's real masses hold the cart down through a tack is a good interaction between creatures and the player. But it only works once the sail-it-yourself step works, and the friends' 'scramble' could easily turn into scripted walks along a plank. The heeling check about the lee wheels is a rig for one axis unless a real rigid body sits under it.

ideas.title: A lamp on the axle: sail into dusk and your speed is your light
ideas.critique: A glowing thing lighting the sand has been done (the hot glass, the burning wire), and the filament is the 'Where I rushed it' wire again. What's new is the chain from wind through the dynamo and circuit to light, read as a pool of light that follows your speed. Without the sailing it is a lamp to watch, nothing more.

ideas.title: The sail is cloth: it bellies in its own flow and rips in a gust
ideas.critique: Two-way cloth and flow with seams that tear would be new physics for the island. But 'a thing loaded until it fails, in slow motion' is the burned-through wire's payoff again, and mending patches is a thin goal. Getting the two-way coupling stable on top of the live box is a large risk for one session.

ideas.title: Pitch the windmill: four cloth sails turning the dynamo on the dune
ideas.critique: The windmill is the charging station of the big goal, so it scores high on toward. As a film it is another machine turning on its own while the camera watches, which is the form the island has repeated ten times. 'Tending it like a fire' is a goal that will mostly be watched, not played.

ideas.title: Forming the lead plates: they fizz while they learn to hold charge
ideas.critique: This is a road step with real Faraday bookkeeping, but the film is one more jar on the bench changing colour by itself under a fixed close camera, the form that is now worth a tenth. A capacity that grows with layer depth will very likely be a fitted curve, and the patient cycling is a chore rather than a game.

ideas.title: A blue spark at the commutator when you break the circuit
ideas.critique: A spark from L di/dt against a breakdown threshold is honest, but it gives one flash in a 5-second film of the bench motor, a device the island has already posted twice. This is the big goal's shared moment cut out early, without the cart that makes it mean something.

ideas.title: Kite traction: fly a cloth kite from the cart and let it drag you
ideas.critique: Steering figure-eights through the wind window to yank the cart is a strong, physical game with a real skill to learn. But it needs the membrane, the rope and the live box all at once, and the likely version is a rigid kite with tabled forces on a line. It is a side road from the electric cart.

ideas.title: Race yesterday: the island's wind is recorded, and you sail against your own ghost
ideas.critique: Racing a ghost car is a standard feature, and it adds no physics beyond what the sailing step brings. Its value is the daily rhythm of the big goal. On its own it is a translucent replay, and the film of a close finish could be staged.

ideas.title: Hike out or go over: the cart lifts two wheels in a gust
ideas.critique: A real rigid-body cart on four sand contacts that tips over by itself is a better base than the tacking idea's heeling check, and riding on two wheels is a thrill a player pushes. It overlaps heavily with the tacking idea and, like it, depends on the sail being live first.
